Building a Cloudflare Worker as an orchestration bridge for GitHub and the Jules Coding Agent is a very sound architectural pattern. Jules works asynchronously inside a cloud VM off GitHub repositories, issues, and PRs, while Cloudflare Workers excel at edge routing, schema validation, and event handling.

---

### System Architecture

```text
               ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
               │              CLOUDFLARE EDGE ORCHESTRATOR             │
               │                                                        │
Client / Chat  │  ┌────────────────────┐      ┌──────────────────────┐  │
 ────────────► │  │  Hono Edge Router  │ ───► │ Workers AI / LLM SDK │  │
               │  └─────────┬──────────┘      └──────────┬───────────┘  │
               │            │                            │ Tool Calls   │
               │            ▼                            ▼              │
               │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
               │  │                Tool Execution Core               │  │
               │  └─────────────┬───────────────────────┬────────────┘  │
               └────────────────┼───────────────────────┼───────────────┘
                                │                       │
                   GitHub REST API Calls        Jules REST API Task Trigger
                                │                       │
                                ▼                       ▼
                      ┌──────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐
                      │   GitHub Org /   │    │   Jules Agent    │
                      │   Repositories   │    │  (Runs VM, Tests,│
                      │  (Create/Update) │    │   Opens PRs)     │
                      └──────────────────┘    └──────────────────┘

```

---

### Core Tools Required for the Worker

The LLM needs a minimal set of deterministic function-calling tools to control the workflow:

* **`create_repo(name, description, private)`**: Calls GitHub API `POST /user/repos` or `POST /orgs/{org}/repos` to provision repositories with `.gitignore` and base templates.
* **`update_repo_files(owner, repo, path, content, message)`**: Uses `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}` to write lockfiles, setup scripts, or configuration files (like `package.json` or `.env.example`).


* **`create_issue(owner, repo, title, body, labels)`**: Posts a bug report, chore, or task specification directly to `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`.
* **`trigger_jules_task(owner, repo, prompt, base_branch)`**: Calls the Jules API endpoint (`POST [https://jules.google/api/v1/sessions](https://jules.google/api/v1/sessions)` or the Jules Action dispatch) with a structured prompt, pointing it to the repository to write code, execute test suites, and open pull requests.



---

### Reference Implementation: `src/index.ts`

This implementation uses **Hono** with Cloudflare Workers and the OpenAI-compatible tool-calling format (which works with Cloudflare Workers AI, Anthropic, or OpenAI endpoints):

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono';

interface Bindings {
  GITHUB_PAT: string;
  JULES_API_KEY: string;
  OPENAI_API_KEY: string;
}

const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: Bindings }>();

// 1. Tool Definitions
const TOOLS = [
  {
    type: 'function',
    function: {
      name: 'create_github_repo',
      description: 'Creates a new repository under the authenticated user or org.',
      parameters: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          name: { type: 'string', description: 'Repository name' },
          description: { type: 'string', description: 'Repository description' },
          is_private: { type: 'boolean', description: 'Whether the repo is private' }
        },
        required: ['name']
      }
    }
  },
  {
    type: 'function',
    function: {
      name: 'trigger_jules_agent',
      description: 'Dispatches a task prompt to the Jules Coding Agent on a target repo.',
      parameters: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          repo: { type: 'string', description: 'Target repo in format owner/repo' },
          prompt: { type: 'string', description: 'Clear specification of what Jules should implement or fix' },
          branch: { type: 'string', description: 'Starting branch (defaults to main)' }
        },
        required: ['repo', 'prompt']
      }
    }
  }
];

// 2. Tool Execution Handlers
async function executeTool(name: string, args: any, env: Bindings) {
  if (name === 'create_github_repo') {
    const res = await fetch('https://api.github.com/user/repos', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${env.GITHUB_PAT}`,
        'User-Agent': 'Cloudflare-Worker-DevOps-Bridge',
        'Accept': 'application/vnd.github+json'
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        name: args.name,
        description: args.description || '',
        private: args.is_private ?? true,
        auto_init: true
      })
    });
    return await res.json();
  }

  if (name === 'trigger_jules_agent') {
    // Dispatch task directly to Jules API
    const res = await fetch('https://jules.google/api/v1/sessions', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${env.JULES_API_KEY}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        repository: args.repo,
        prompt: args.prompt,
        starting_branch: args.branch || 'main'
      })
    });
    return await res.json();
  }

  throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${name}`);
}

// 3. Orchestration Endpoint
app.post('/api/orchestrate', async (c) => {
  const { instructions } = await c.req.json();
  const env = c.env;

  // Step 1: Query the model with tool capabilities
  const initialPayload = {
    model: 'gpt-4o', // Or call c.env.AI.run() for Cloudflare Workers AI
    messages: [
      {
        role: 'system',
        content: 'You are a devops assistant capable of managing GitHub repositories and delegating coding tasks to Jules.'
      },
      { role: 'user', content: instructions }
    ],
    tools: TOOLS,
    tool_choice: 'auto'
  };

  const aiResponse = await fetch('https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${env.OPENAI_API_KEY}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(initialPayload)
  });

  const aiData: any = await aiResponse.json();
  const message = aiData.choices[0].message;

  // Step 2: Handle Tool Invocations
  if (message.tool_calls && message.tool_calls.length > 0) {
    const toolResults = [];

    for (const toolCall of message.tool_calls) {
      const toolName = toolCall.function.name;
      const toolArgs = JSON.parse(toolCall.function.arguments);
      const executionOutput = await executeTool(toolName, toolArgs, env);

      toolResults.push({
        tool_call_id: toolCall.id,
        role: 'tool',
        name: toolName,
        content: JSON.stringify(executionOutput)
      });
    }

    return c.json({
      status: 'executed',
      message: message.content,
      toolResults
    });
  }

  return c.json({ status: 'completed', response: message.content });
});

export default app;

```

### Essential Constraints & Setup

* **GitHub Token Permissions**: Use a GitHub fine-grained PAT or GitHub App installation token restricted solely to the organization or repos it needs to govern. Grant `Administration: read/write` (for repo creation) and `Contents: read/write` + `Issues: read/write`.


* **Prompt Framing for Jules**: Jules performs best when given structured constraints (e.g., acceptance criteria, test files to run, explicit directory trees). Ensure the system prompt formats instructions for Jules into self-contained markdown specs before firing the tool.


* **Secrets Configuration**: Store `GITHUB_PAT`, `JULES_API_KEY`, and LLM keys via `wrangler secret put <KEY_NAME>` so sensitive tokens are never exposed in source code.

In the 23-pod studio topology, **POD-12** is staffed by a DevOps Engineer and an Automation Engineer whose mandate is configuring Cloudflare Workers, R2 buckets, and agent orchestration (specifically calling out tools like Jules).

* **Automated CI/CD Fixes & Dependency Bumps:** When **POD-06 (Data Ops)** flags an updated base checkpoint or node package regression, the Worker can direct Jules to fork the repo, create an isolated branch, patch TypeScript types or Python requirements, and open a PR with the golden-set test run.

### 3. Git-Backed Corpus Ingestion & Audit Trails

The studio uses Git repositories (such as `@snailicid3/consumer-npm` and `/codex/`) as the legislative assembly of canonical universe facts:

* **Automated Scene AST Commits:** Once Child Graph A generates the screenplay `.fountain` file and the `dialogue_ast.json`, the Worker's GitHub tool commits them directly to the episode branch (e.g., `feat/ep101-sc03`).


* **Dirty-State Invalidation:** Pushing these commits via GitHub API triggers GitHub Actions, updating the canonical state hash in Cloudflare D1 and flagging downstream scenes that touch altered facts as `is_dirty = 1`.


* **Jules as the Invariant Patching Agent:** If an Invariant Linter or Vitest schema check fails during a PR run (e.g., a character's injured arm was referenced as functional), the Worker can prompt Jules with the linter diff to refactor the broken scene AST programmatically before human sign-off.

### 4. Task Handoff & Edge Orchestration

The Worker coordinates the decoupled handoffs across the Generative Core:

* **Locking the Audio Grid:** When Child Graph B outputs the dialogue `.wav` stems and `locked_schedule.json`, the Worker updates the repository and triggers the Remotion animatic build.


* **Gating the Generative Core (POD-15):** The Worker enforces the human sign-off gate. Once the showrunner greenlights the animatic in the Astro dashboard, the Worker's orchestration endpoint instantiates the `ShotCoordinator` Durable Object to dispatch frame-accurate greenscreen plates to RunPod Serverless.

### Recommended Pick

If you want immediate consistency across your existing documents and repo configs, use **`edge-director`** (or `pod12-edge-director` in monorepo directories).

If this service is specifically deployed *only* to bridge GitHub tasks and Jules sessions, **`jules-dispatcher`** or **`stilus-scribe`** gives it an unmistakable operational identity.**Yes, absolutely.** It must be completely separate from the locked `edge-director` (POD-12’s edge middleware).

Combining an experimental, tool-calling LLM that writes Git code and delegates to Jules into the same Worker running your production middleware introduces an avoidable blast-radius failure mode.

---

### The Separation of Responsibilities

| Dimension | POD-12 Production Middleware (`edge-director`) | The DevOps Agent Bridge (`jules-dispatcher` / `stilus-scribe`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Operational Role** | The **Line Producer / Stage Manager** (The live production pipe).

 | The **Meta-Tool / Scaffolding Mechanic** (The pipeline developer).

 |
| **Runtime Criticality** | **Tier 3 (Structural Execution):** If it goes down, rendering stops, sockets drop, and artists cannot queue shots.

 | **Out-of-Band (Chore / Developer Tool):** If it crashes or loops, the media production floor runs unaffected.

 |
| **Execution Pattern** | Deterministic, sub-5ms routing, single-threaded DO mutexes, and zero-downtime WebSocket hibernation.

 | Stochastic ReAct loops, multi-second LLM tool-calling roundtrips, and long-running git operations.

 |
| **Secrets & Permissions** | Read-only access to Cloudflare D1 canon checks, signed R2 pre-signed URLs, and job lease tokens.

 | Write/Admin tokens for GitHub (`Contents: write`, `Pull Requests: write`, `Repo creation`) and Jules execution keys.

 |

### Why the Blast Radius Demands Isolation

* **Credential Segregation (Least Privilege):** If an agent prompt injection occurs, or an LLM hallucination enters a tool loop, `edge-director` only holds D1 read tokens and queue leases. The GitHub/Jules bridge must hold elevated Git PATs to create and push repositories. You must never expose administrative repository write keys within the live render-traffic isolate.


* **CPU & Timeout Contention:** Cloudflare Workers running standard API proxies execute within tight CPU burst profiles. Running recursive LLM ReAct loops that wait on external GitHub commits and Jules VM dispatches will easily exhaust edge execution envelopes, risking latency spikes or process kills on your active render queues.


* **Decoupled Failure Domains:** As established in your Pod specs, POD-12 has the broadest simultaneous blast radius in the studio. Tying live media dispatch to an experimental coding meta-tool violates the core boundary rule: *meta-tooling must never be in the critical path of runtime asset rendering*.

### 1. Automating the "Git-for-Canon" Assembly Line

`cinema-gen.00.md` defines narrative canon as a version-controlled state machine where writers propose changes via pull requests to `@snailicid3/consumer-npm` and pin versions using lockfiles.

* **Autonomous Proposal PRs:** When a writer or sub-agent locks a scene premise in the Astro UI, `repo-bot` uses the GitHub API to fork/branch the repository, commit the extracted markdown frontmatter and scene AST, and open a pull request (e.g., `feat/ep101-sc03`).


* **Dirty-State Git Commits:** When an upstream Fact node mutates (e.g., a character loses an item or sustains an injury), `repo-bot` receives the D1 webhook and writes automated chore commits (`chore(codex): flag dirty scenes downstream of fact_020`).


* **Merge Queue Sanitation:** `repo-bot` can enforce the "Merge Master" rules, rejecting or merging dependency updates across rooms without requiring manual branch management from creative leads.

### 2. Autonomous Invariant Patching with Jules

The document specifies strict pre-commit and CI linters (Vitest schemas, syllable-to-frame calculators, and $O(1)$ set-intersection kinetic verb linters) designed to catch physical impossibilities at $T_0$ ($0.00 cost).

When human writers or drafting tools commit invalid scenes that trip these gates, `repo-bot` steps in to triage the failure:

```text
[ GitHub Action: Invariant Check Fails ]
                   │

```

* **Surgical Minimal Enclosing Unit (MEU) Patching:** `cinema-gen.00.md` warns against full-scene re-rolls, which introduce non-deterministic drift. `repo-bot` sends the exact linter diff and scene AST coordinates to Jules, instructing it to patch only the offending kinetic verb or frontmatter reference rather than regenerating the chapter.

`cinema-gen.00.md` explicitly warns:

`repo-bot` directly complies with this philosophy. It does not attempt to write complex code, understand the narrative lore, or act as an all-knowing compiler. It remains a lightweight edge webhook handler that does two basic mechanical things:

1. Calls the standard GitHub REST API to manage branches, files, and tags.


2. Delegates any complex codebase modification, script scaffolding, or linter repair directly to the Jules sandbox environment.



This provides all the leverage of automated repo management while keeping your production pipeline completely decoupled from experimental coding models.The **"Git-for-Canon" Assembly Line** treats worldbuilding and narrative continuity not as qualitative prose documents, but as an append-only, version-controlled state machine. ### 1. The Data Model: Atomic Entity Files and Frontmatter Contracts

To avoid merge collisions when multiple writers, directors, or sub-agents draft concurrently, the narrative universe is decomposed into atomic files rather than a single monolithic story bible:

* **Atomic Entity Files:** Every character, location, faction, and core world law lives in its own isolated Markdown/YAML file within the repository (e.g., `corpus/characters/char_020_the_pilot.md`). Two writers can update different character dossiers simultaneously without triggering Git merge conflicts.


* **Frontmatter Dependency Pins:** When a scene is authored, its dependencies are not stored in conversational prompts; they are declared directly in the scene document’s YAML frontmatter:


```yaml
---
id: "ep101_sc01"
title: "Culvert Siphon Stash"
status: "CLEAN"
depends_on:
  - fact_id: "fact_the_pilot_hand_injury"
    pinned_version: 1
  - fact_id: "loc_sector_4_culvert"
    pinned_version: 3
---

```


This explicit structure binds the scene AST to immutable integer versions of upstream narrative facts.


* **Two-Pass Compilation:** The repository contains a two-pass Zod compiler. Pass 1 parses individual entity schemas; Pass 2 walks the entire relational graph to verify referential integrity, ensuring zero orphaned pointers across all 60+ entities before compiling `compiled/bible-state.json`.

```text
              ▼
    [ GitHub Repository: @snailicid3/consumer-npm ]
              │
              ▼ (Triggers GitHub Actions)
    [ CI Gauntlet: .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml ]
              ├── npm run check:ts (Type safety)
              ├── npm test (Vitest schema validation)
              └── npm run compile (Graph pointer check)

```

1. **Branch Provisioning:** When a writer begins a beat, `repo-bot` cuts an isolated feature branch (`feat/ep101-sc03-siphon`) from `main`.


2. **Dual-Artifact Serialization:** Once Child Graph A generates the screenplay text and the structured dialogue AST, `repo-bot` formats them into the dual-artifact: the human-readable `ep101_sc03.fountain` screenplay and the machine-readable `dialogue_ast.json`.


3. **Autonomous PR Submission:** `repo-bot` writes the files, stages the commit, and opens a GitHub Pull Request with an automated summary detailing which character somatic baselines, locations, and inventories are engaged.



---

### 3. The Pre-Merge CI Gauntlet and Invariant Linters

Under the Git-for-Canon model, no lore changes can be pushed directly to `main`. Branch protection rules and pre-commit hooks enforce a strict compilation gauntlet:

* **TypeScript & Schema Validation:** CI executes `npm run check:ts` and `npm test` using Vitest to ensure all mutated entities match the strict Zod specifications for somatic, logistical, and epistemic state vectors.


* **Zero Orphaned Pointers:** `npm run compile` executes against the entire corpus. If a writer deletes or renames an inventory item (e.g., `poly_drum_01`) that another scene's frontmatter references as an active dependency, the compiler fails, blocking the PR.


* **Deterministic Invariant Linter:** Pre-merge checks run an $O(1)$ set-intersection check against kinetic action verbs. If an injured character (e.g., The Pilot with a severed brachial plexus) is described as performing an impossible physical verb (such as "vaults" or "climbs two-handed"), CI halts the pull request at $T_0$ before any GPU compute is allocated.



---

### 4. Dirty-State Propagation & Git Audit Trails

When a foundational fact mutates, `repo-bot` prevents silent narrative drift by operationalizing cache invalidation across the Git tree:

```text
[ Showrunner Merges PR: Fact #020 mutates v2 -> v3 ]
                       │
                       ▼
         [ Cloudflare D1 State Ledger ]
                       │
                       ▼ (D1 SQL Invalidation Query)
    Identifies 3 Downstream Scenes with pinned_version < 3
                       │
                       ▼ (Webhook to repo-bot)
         ┌───────────────────────────┐
         │         repo-bot          │
         └─────────────┬─────────────┘
                       │
       ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
       ▼                               ▼
[ Automated Chore Commits ]   [ Issue / PR Warning Flags ]
"chore(codex): flag dirty     "⚠️ Canon Breach: Scene 04
 scenes downstream of fact20"   pinned to obsolete arm v2"

```

1. **Version Increment:** An approved edit to a fact (e.g., The Pilot losing his arm in Episode 1) increments its integer version from `v2` to `v3` in Cloudflare D1.


2. **Dependency Query:** An indexed SQL query sweeps `scene_fact_dependencies` to locate all downstream scenes pinned to version `v2`.


3. **Automated Chore Commits:** `repo-bot` receives the invalidation payload and writes automated commits to active draft branches: `chore(codex): flag dirty scenes downstream of fact_020`.


4. **Halting the Pipeline:** `repo-bot` flips the status of affected scene files from `CLEAN` to `DIRTY` with a diff string explaining the collision, programmatically locking the render pipeline and preventing serverless GPU dispatch until a writer reconciles the text.



---

### 5. Cross-Room Versioning, Lockfiles, and Optimistic Concurrency

When multiple production pods or spin-off writers' rooms work within the shared universe, `repo-bot` manages distributed state resolution:

* **The `canon.lock` Manifest:** Similar to `package-lock.json` in software, each episode or production room maintains an explicit lockfile. Instead of pointing to floating fact references, a scene binds to an immutable cryptographic snapshot: `Scene_14 -> Fact_Node_042@sha256:8f434...`. A retcon merged by Room A does not silently break Room B's in-flight work until Room B deliberately upgrades its pinned manifest.


* **Optimistic Concurrency Control:** To prevent bureaucratic latency where writers are blocked waiting for continuity approvals, the system allows **Provisional Edges**. A writer can draft against an unapproved fact proposal; `repo-bot` commits the scene tagged as `Provisional: Pending Upstream Merge`. If the Showrunner approves the fact, the provisional tag clears automatically; if rejected, `repo-bot` flags the scene as dirty, requiring a rewrite.


* **The Continuity Merge Master:** A designated Continuity Producer (POD-11) owns the `main` trunk, using `repo-bot` to review, adjudicate, and merge canon updates across the entire studio network.



---

### 6. Closing the Loop: State Delta Commits to `/codex/`

Once an episode scene passes director review and completes its final Remotion composite, the loop is closed by archiving reality back into Git:

* **State Delta Emission:** The completed execution emits two final artifacts: the conformed screenplay and a `state_delta.json` recording every resource consumed, wound taken, or secret revealed during the action.


* **Codex Commit:** `repo-bot` commits this delta directly into the `/codex/` repository (e.g., `git commit -am "chore(codex): pilot state delta post-ep101-sc01"`).


* **Snapshot Ingestion:** The commit triggers an update to Cloudflare D1's `canon_state_snapshots`, establishing the newly verified world state as the baseline for all subsequent episodes.Autonomous Invariant Patching shifts continuity remediation from an expensive downstream human or GPU problem down to an asynchronous, zero-cost edge loop ($T_0$).

Instead of re-rolling entire scenes—which introduces non-deterministic drift that breaks adjacent dialogue, staging, and continuity—the pipeline pairs the **Deterministic Invariant Linter** with the **Jules Coding Agent** via `repo-bot` to execute surgical, mathematically bounded patches directly against the repository.

---

### 1. The Interception Gate ($T_0$ AST Audit)

Before text-to-speech synthesis or GPU diffusion is permitted, Child Graph A emits a dual-artifact: a human-readable screenplay (`.fountain`) and a machine-readable Abstract Syntax Tree (`dialogue_ast.json`) containing discrete `extracted_motor_actions`.

The Invariant Linter intercepts this AST and runs three deterministic audits:

```text
               CANDIDATE SCENE AST (From Child Graph A)
                                  │
                                  ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   LAYER 1 INVARIANT LINTER                       │
│                                                                  │
│  1. Somatic Audit: AST_Actions ∩ Somatic.banned_kinetic_verbs     │
│  2. Logistical Audit: Free hands vs. held items & item leases    │
│  3. Epistemic Audit: Dialogue tokens vs. unlearned secrets       │
└─────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                  ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                  ▼ PASSED                        ▼ FAILED
        [ Release to TTS / GPU ]       [ Emit Diagnostic Error Payload ]
                                                  │
                                                  ▼
                                     [ Webhook Dispatched to repo-bot ]

```

When an invariant fails (e.g., an injured character with a severed brachial plexus is scripted performing a two-handed heave or sprint), the linter does not emit a vague text warning. It halts execution and emits a structured JSON diagnostic coordinate:

```json
{
  "scene_id": "ep101_sc03",
  "file_path": "scenes/ep101_sc03.json",
  "target_type": "SOMATIC_VIOLATION",
  "character_id": "char_020_the_pilot",
  "shot_index": 2,
  "paragraph_index": 4,
  "lines": [12, 16],
  "breached_token": "SPRINT_TO_SLED",
  "active_condition": "brachial_plexus_severed",
  "banned_verbs": ["sprint", "vault", "climb", "heave_two_handed"],
  "allowed_alternatives": ["drag_leg", "brace_arm", "asymmetric_slog"]
}

```

---

### 2. The Minimal Enclosing Unit (MEU) Scoping Engine

Before delegating the fix to Jules, the system calculates the **Minimal Enclosing Unit (MEU)** boundary $[I_{\text{start}}, I_{\text{end}}]$. A paragraph or shot cannot simply be patched in isolation if downstream beats contain references or callbacks to physical states introduced within that unit.

```text
Paragraph 1: Silas leans against the wet sluice gate. [STABLE PREFIX]
Paragraph 2: Silas draws the brass siphon from his oilskin coat. [STABLE PREFIX]
Paragraph 3: [FATAL BREACH: Silas sprints across the mud toward the pump]
Paragraph 4: He attaches the siphon nozzle to the bleeder valve. [DEPENDENT TARGET]
Paragraph 5: The pump engine coughs black exhaust. [STABLE SUFFIX]

       ◄─── Backward Scan ───►                 ◄─── Forward Scan ───►
      Anchor Prefix: Paragraph 2              Dependent Target: Paragraph 4
      
              EXPANDED REPAIR WINDOW = [ Paragraph 3 + Paragraph 4 ]

```

* **Backward Scan (Upstream Closure):** Inspects preceding units to locate the prerequisite anchor (e.g., verifying that the siphon was already drawn in Paragraph 2).


* **Forward Scan (Downstream Closure):** Scans downstream units for entities introduced in the broken unit. Because Paragraph 4 relies on Silas reaching the valve, the repair window expands to encapsulate both Paragraph 3 and Paragraph 4.


* **The Infill Anchor Contract:** The prompt explicitly locks Paragraph 1–2 as an **Immutable Prefix** and Paragraph 5 as an **Immutable Suffix**, forcing the repair to fit seamlessly between them.



---

### 3. `repo-bot` Task Formulation & Jules Dispatch

`repo-bot` captures the MEU context and linter diagnostics, formats them into a strict task specification, and dispatches it to the Jules Coding Agent API:

```typescript
// repo-bot/src/tools/julesDispatcher.ts
export async function dispatchJulesInvariantPatch(
  diagnostics: LinterViolation, 
  meu: MinimalEnclosingUnit, 
  env: Bindings
) {
  const taskPrompt = `
# REPAIR SPECIFICATION: INVARIANT VIOLATION (${diagnostics.target_type})
Target Repo: @snailicid3/consumer-npm
Target File: ${diagnostics.file_path}
Target Branch: feat/${diagnostics.scene_id}-repair

## 1. Context & Problem
In shot ${diagnostics.shot_index}, entity '${diagnostics.character_id}' attempted prohibited action '${diagnostics.breached_token}'.
Active Condition: ${diagnostics.active_condition}.

## 2. Hard Infill Constraints
- IMMUTABLE PREFIX:
"""
${meu.immutable_prefix}
"""
- IMMUTABLE SUFFIX:
"""
${meu.immutable_suffix}
"""

## 3. Surgical Directive
Rewrite ONLY lines ${diagnostics.lines[0]}-${diagnostics.lines[1]} (Paragraphs ${meu.start}-${meu.end}).
- Eliminate '${diagnostics.breached_token}' and banned verbs: [${diagnostics.banned_verbs.join(', ')}].
- Substitute valid motor locomotion matching: [${diagnostics.allowed_alternatives.join(', ')}].
- Ensure Silas arrives at the bleeder valve to preserve the downstream dependency of Paragraph 4.
- Do not alter character knowledge or dialogue secrets.

## 4. Verification Mandate
Run 'npm test tests/invariants.test.ts' and 'npm run compile'. 
Ensure zero type errors and zero invariant violations before committing.
`;

  return await fetch('https://jules.google/api/v1/sessions', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${env.JULES_API_KEY}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      repository: diagnostics.repo,
      starting_branch: `feat/${diagnostics.scene_id}`,
      task_description: taskPrompt
    })
  });
}

```

### 4. Sandboxed VM Execution & Verification Inside Jules

Jules executes within an isolated VM container, operating under the same rules as an engineering collaborator:

1. **Repository Checkout:** Jules clones the active scene branch (`feat/ep101-sc03`) inside its VM.


2. **File Modification:** Jules reads the AST and screenplay files, locates the exact coordinate offsets, and modifies only the targeted paragraphs within the defined MEU window.


3. **Local Test Suite Execution:** Rather than assuming the patch works, Jules runs the local test runner:
```bash
npm run canon:lint -- scenes/ep101_sc03.json
npm test tests/invariants.test.ts

```




4.  **Two-Pass Compilation Check:** Jules runs `npm run compile` to verify that no entity pointers were broken elsewhere in the narrative relational graph.
5.  **Automated PR Commit:** Once the linter passes with exit code `0`, Jules pushes the clean commit (`fix(canon): patch somatic motor violation in shot 02`) to the branch.

### 5. Convergence vs. Divergence: The Circuit Breaker

Automated patching cannot be permitted to loop indefinitely. The system uses the **Three-Cycle Escalation Rule** and monitors error trajectory across attempts:

```text
                     [ Invariant Linter Flags Violation ]
                                      │
                                      ▼
                        [ Execute Jules Patch (Cycle 1) ]
                                      │
                             Did linter pass?
                             ┌────────┴────────┐
                             ▼ YES             ▼ NO
                        [ Commit PR ]   [ Analyze Trajectory ]
                                               │
                       ┌───────────────────────┴───────────────────────┐
                       ▼ CONVERGENCE                                   ▼ DIVERGENCE
          (Phrasing basin: 'sprint' -> 'dash')            (Error jumped: somatic -> inventory)
                       │                                               │
            [ Allow Jules Cycle 2 ]                            [ HARD PIPELINE HALT ]
                       │                                       • Abort autonomous loops
            Passes on micro-prompt?                            • Tag #ESCALATED_CONFLICT
                 ┌─────┴─────┐                                 • Route diagnostic dossier
                 ▼ YES       ▼ NO                                to Story Architect
            [ Commit ]  [ HARD HALT ]

```

* **Convergence (Local Phrasing Basin):** If Attempt 2 fails with a near-identical error (e.g., swapping "sprinted" for "dashed"), the model is in a localized semantic rut. `repo-bot` re-prompts Jules with an amplified negative constraint list.


* **Divergence (Structural Conflict):** If Attempt 2 fixes the physical motion but creates an inventory impossibility (e.g., Silas puts away the siphon to crawl, meaning he no longer holds the tool in Paragraph 4), the constraints are **mutually exclusive**.


* **The Escape Hatch:** The moment divergence is detected, the patch loop breaks immediately. The task status flips to `BLOCKED`, and `repo-bot` routes an escalation dossier (containing the constraint matrix, diff history, and contradiction logs) to the **Tier 2 Story Architect** in ClickUp/Astro, preventing wasted compute on an impossible plot geometry.The Pre-Merge CI Gauntlet and Invariant Linters form the deterministic boundary separating authorial/LLM intent from downstream rendering compute. By evaluating narrative, somatic, and logistical constraints at compile time ($T_0$), defects are arrested before audio synthesis (Child Graph B) or GPU plate generation (Child Graph C) can consume production budget.

### 1. The Pre-Merge CI Workflow (`validate-bible.yml`)

The static corpus repository (`goblin-bible` / `@snailicid3/consumer-npm`) acts as "The Law". Branch protection rules on `main` prevent direct pushes, requiring all lore mutations to pass an automated multi-step verification pipeline:

```yaml
name: Validate Bible

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Run validation (schema + integrity)
        run: npx tsx scripts/validate.ts
      - name: Run test suite
        run: npx vitest run
      - name: Run voice-bleed lint
        run: npx tsx scripts/lint-voice.ts
      - name: Compile and check for uncommitted drift
        run: |
          npx tsx scripts/compile.ts
          git diff --exit-code compiled/ || {
            echo "::error::compiled/ output doesn't match source. Run 'npx tsx scripts/compile.ts' and commit the result.";
            exit 1;
          }

```

* **`scripts/validate.ts`**: Verifies that every Markdown file parses against its Zod schema and confirms cross-reference integrity before serialization.


* **`scripts/lint-voice.ts`**: Flags lexical and dialogue overlap across character callback phrases to arrest voice bleed at authoring time.


* **Drift Check (`git diff --exit-code compiled/`)**: Asserts that `compiled/bible-state.json` matches the markdown source exactly, preventing uncompiled draft drift from being merged into the canonical trunk.



---

### 2. The Two-Pass Corpus Compiler (`scripts/compile.ts`)

The compiler converts markdown files with YAML frontmatter into a single, byte-identical JSON state ledger. Downstream runtimes never parse raw Markdown; they consume only this compiled artifact.

```text
/characters/*.md  ──┐
/grievances/*.md  ──┼─► [ Pass 1: Shape Validation ] ─► [ Pass 2: Relational Sweeps ] ─► [ Pass 3: Deterministic Seal ]
/locations/*.md   ──┤        (Zod Schemas)                 (DAG / Pointer Checks)           (Alphabetical Sort + SHA-256)
/possessions/*.md ──┘                                                                                  │
                                                                                                       ▼
                                                                                           compiled/bible-state.json

```

* **Pass 1 (Shape & Scalar Bounds):** Uses `gray-matter` and Zod to validate field definitions. It enforces numeric ranges (e.g., condition severity $0.0 \le s \le 1.0$, escalation ceilings $1 \le c \le 5$, base stats $1 \le b \le 5$) and enum memberships (`LocomotionBaselineEnum`, `RelationshipType`). Duplicate entity IDs throw immediate `DUPLICATE_ID` fatal exits.


* **Pass 2 (Relational Integrity & DAG Cycle Detection):** Validates all foreign keys across the relational corpus. Every equip slot (`held`, `worn`, `carried`, `cached`) must resolve to a valid possession file; every participant and string target must point to an active character. A depth-first search (DFS) with recursion stack tracking audits `spawns_grievances` to mathematically reject circular spawn loops (`CYCLE_DETECTED`).


* **Pass 3 (Deterministic Sealing):** Object keys are sorted alphabetically via recursive traversal. Dynamic runtime timestamps (`new Date().toISOString()`) are strictly forbidden to preserve hash determinism. The compiler hashes the canonical string using SHA-256 and executes an atomic write (`.tmp_*` file rename) to `compiled/bible-state.json`.



---

### 3. Layer 0: Combinatorial Satisfiability (SAT) Pre-Flight

Before an LLM or author drafts a scene, the Pre-Flight SAT Engine evaluates whether requested actions are mathematically satisfiable given the character's active state vectors in Cloudflare D1.

```typescript
// src/hub/preflightSAT.ts
import { SomaticVector, LogisticalVector, EpistemicVector } from '../schemas';

export interface ActionPreconditions {
  actor_id: string;
  required_free_hands: number;
  required_kinetic_verbs: string[];
  required_unspoken_secrets: string[];
}

export class PreflightSATEngine {
  public static verify(
    prereqs: ActionPreconditions,
    somatic: SomaticVector,
    logistics: LogisticalVector,
    epistemic: EpistemicVector
  ): { satisfiable: boolean; unsatisfiable_reasons: string[] } {
    const failures: string[] = [];

    // Hand Capacity Invariant: sum(occupied) <= 2 - impairment_penalty
    const occupiedHands = logistics.slots.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.occupies_hands, 0);
    const availableHands = 2 - occupiedHands - (somatic.hand_impairment_penalty ?? 0);
    if (prereqs.required_free_hands > availableHands) {
      failures.push(
        `HAND_OVERLOAD: Action requires ${prereqs.required_free_hands} free hands. ` +
        `Entity [${prereqs.actor_id}] has ${availableHands} available.`
      );
    }

    // Kinetic Limits (Somatic Invariants)
    for (const verb of prereqs.required_kinetic_verbs) {
      if (somatic.banned_kinetic_verbs.includes(verb)) {
        failures.push(
          `SOMATIC_VIOLATION: Verb [${verb}] forbidden by baseline ` +
          `[${somatic.locomotion_baseline}] on [${prereqs.actor_id}].`
        );
      }
    }

    // Epistemic Preconditions
    for (const secretId of prereqs.required_unspoken_secrets) {
      if (!epistemic.known_secrets.some(s => s.secret_id === secretId)) {
        failures.push(`EPISTEMIC_DEFICIT: Secret [${secretId}] unrevealed to [${prereqs.actor_id}].`);
      }
    }

    return { satisfiable: failures.length === 0, unsatisfiable_reasons: failures };
  }
}

```

If an entity lacks physical hand capacity ($\sum s.\text{occupies\_hands} > 2.0 - \text{penalty}$) or attempts an impossible action, the SAT solver proves unsatisfiability and terminates execution at $T_0$, consuming zero GPU tokens.

### 4. Layer 1: The AST Invariant Linter & Self-Healing Loop

When Child Graph A generates scene blocking, GBNF grammar constraints force the LLM to emit a dual-artifact: a human-readable screenplay (`.fountain`) and a machine-readable JSON AST containing discrete `extracted_motor_actions`.

```json
{
  "shot_id": "sh_02",
  "character_id": "char_020_the_pilot",
  "screenplay_action": "The Pilot heaves the drum and sprints toward the sled.",
  "extracted_motor_actions": ["HEAVE_DRUM", "SPRINT_TO_SLED"],
  "dialogue_text": "Get the line cleared!"
}

```

```typescript
// src/services/invariantLinter.ts
export function lintSceneAST(
  shots: ASTShot[],
  somaticProfiles: Record<string, SomaticVector>
): { passed: boolean; violations: string[] } {
  const violations: string[] = [];

  for (const shot of shots) {
    const profile = somaticProfiles[shot.character_id];
    if (!profile) continue;

    // Direct O(1) Set-Intersection
    const illegalActions = shot.extracted_motor_actions.filter((action) =>
      profile.banned_kinetic_verbs.includes(action)
    );

    if (illegalActions.length > 0) {
      violations.push(
        `[INVARIANT VIOLATION] Character '${shot.character_id}' executed prohibited motor actions ` +
        `[${illegalActions.join(', ')}] in shot '${shot.shot_id}'.`
      );
    }
  }

  return { passed: violations.length === 0, violations };
}

```

```text
[ Child Graph A Output ] ──► [ O(1) Set-Intersection Linter ] ──► [ Secondary Verb-Lemma Scan ]
                                          │                                    │
                                   Violations Found                     Discrepancy Found
                                          │                                    │
                                          ▼                                    ▼
                               ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                               │               SURGICAL REPAIR DISPATCH                 │
                               │  Negative Directive: "Pilot has lumbar pinch; cannot  │
                               │  sprint. Replace with asymmetric ground drag."         │
                               └──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                                                          │
                                                          ▼
                                            [ Regenerate Candidate Take ]

```

* **Dual Audit Tripwire:** Self-reported AST enums are paired with a secondary verb-lemma prose scan. If the model self-reports `extracted_motor_actions: ["LIMP"]` but writes *"he sprinted"* in the action line, the divergence trips the compiler gate.


* **Self-Healing Loop:** Violations are caught automatically by the orchestrator, formatted into explicit surgical constraints, and reinjected into the generator context for an immediate Take 2 without human intervention.

### 5. Deterministic Gating vs. Advisory Lints

The system strictly bifurcates rules into blocking compilation errors and advisory editorial scores:

| Verification Stage | Gate Type | Enforcement Mechanism | Failure Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Corpus Relational Integrity**<br> | **Hard Gate**<br> | Vitest / Zod schema compiler (`scripts/compile.ts`)

 | CI failure; PR blocked; `compiled/` artifacts not written.

 |
| **Somatic & Motor Limits**<br> | **Hard Gate**<br> | $O(1)$ set intersection against `banned_kinetic_verbs`<br> | Pipeline halt at $T_0$; zero audio synthesis or GPU plate dispatch.

 |
| **Logistical Slot Conservation**<br> | **Hard Gate**<br> | Capacity arithmetic ($\sum \text{occupies\_hands} \le 2.0 - \text{penalty}$)

 | Job rejection; mandatory inventory reconciliations.

 |
| **Epistemic Third-Rails**<br> | **Hard Gate**<br> | Dialogue token scan against secret escalation ceilings

 | Scene AST quarantine; automatic repair loop dispatch.

 |
| **Monetization & Ad-Suitability**<br> | **Hard Gate**<br> | Boolean rule-matching on gore, violence, and foley schemas

 | Red Flag classification; generation halted before diffusion.

 |
| **MRU Prose Syntax**<br> | **Advisory**<br> | Dependency parsing checking Stimulus $\to$ Feeling $\to$ Reflex $\to$ Action

 | Logged as advisory warning; never blocks pipeline progression.

 |

**Auteur Overrides as Bug Telemetry:** When human authors use an override to bypass advisory rules, the action is recorded in `linter_override_telemetry`. If a specific syntax or pacing rule accumulates a high bypass frequency (e.g., bypassed 45+ times across production cycles), the rule is flagged as obsolete and refactored by the engineering lead, preventing the pipeline from enforcing flawed constraints.Phase 5 operates completely out-of-band from the linear, episode-by-episode production floor. While the active line rushes to lock scripts, synthesize audio, and render shots, the **Background Meta-Loop & Canaries** run an asynchronous feedback cycle that refines diffusion models, polishes sampling envelopes, and prevents silent semantic and infrastructure drift over time.

---

### 1. The Continuous Model Refinement Engine (Human Gates 4 & 5)

Rather than treating models and LoRAs as static artifacts, the pipeline uses its own production exhaust to systematically distill specialized downstream weights.

```text
[ Active Generative Core ] ──► [ Multimodal Critic Evaluation ]
                                          │
                  ┌───────────────────────┴───────────────────────┐
                  ▼ S >= 0.92 (High Quality)                      ▼ Severe Failure
         [ /staging/ Bucket ]                            [ Negative Guidance Buffer ]
                  │                                      • Tagged prompt/latent pairs
                  ▼                                      • Prevents Model Autophagy (MAD)
    [ Uncertainty-Weighted Sampling ]
    (High variance -> Human Gate 4)
                  │
                  ▼ Cleared
          [ /golden/ Dataset ] 
                  │ (Accumulates 200–250 verified pairs)
                  ▼
         [ Automated Retraining ] ──► (Kohya / Modal / Serverless Worker)
                  │
                  ▼
      [ Shadow Canary Bake-Off ] ──► 100 headless runs against baseline
                  │
                  ▼ Pass
      [ Human Gate 5: Promotion ] ──► Lead designer sign-off & hot-reload

```

* **Experience Ledger Recording:** Every inference run logs its exact deterministic parameters (seed, steps, CFG, scheduler), cryptographic hashes (base weights, LoRAs, DAG JSON), and the full critic manifest to a relational store. Bayesian optimizers query this ledger to continuously refine default parameter boundaries per scene aesthetic.


* **Uncertainty-Weighted Active Sampling (Human Gate 4):** Generations clearing the quality threshold ($S \ge 0.92$) are staged for dataset inclusion. Instead of auditing a purely random sample, the system evaluates model entropy by querying the Video-LLM across three passes at $T=0.7$. High-confidence, unanimous passes move directly to `/golden/`; high-variance or borderline judgments are routed to the human supervisor’s review queue.


* **Negative Exemplar Buffering:** Failed generations are preserved in a dedicated buffer with explicit failure tags. Retaining these failure cases counteracts distribution collapse and prevents Model Autophagy Disorder (MAD) during retraining cycles.


* **Shadow Canary Bake-Offs (Human Gate 5):** Once `/golden/` reaches 200–250 verified pairs, an automated serverless job trains a candidate adapter (maintaining a 60/40 human-anchor to synthetic ratio). Before entering production, the candidate must pass 100 headless shadow canary runs against a baseline prompt suite. If hard-gate failure rates spike $>10\%$, the candidate is automatically quarantined; if stable, it is presented via an A/B matrix to the visual lead for cryptographic sign-off.



---

### 2. Zero-Trust Critic Auditing & Synthetic Canaries

Because Video-LLMs are non-deterministic and subject to silent provider weight updates, the evaluation layer cannot be naively trusted to grade itself.

```text
[ Active Evaluation Queue ]
             │
             ├── Every Nth Job: Inject Synthetic Defect
             │   ├── Corrupt limb geometry into 3 frames
             │   └── Splice out-of-context asset (e.g., modern sedan in rural noir)
             │
             ▼
[ Multi-Tier Critic Pipeline ]
             │
     ┌───────┴───────┐
     ▼ Caught        ▼ Missed
[ Pass Job ]   [ CRITIC COMPROMISED ]
               • Retraining pipeline halts immediately
               • Critic permissions downgraded to logging-only
               • Automated webhook alerts platform engineering

```

* **Synthetic Canary Insertion:** The system programmatically injects deliberate, unmistakable errors (such as impossible physical shears or anachronistic objects) into every $N$-th job in the evaluation stream.


* **The Compromise Circuit Breaker:** If the automated critic fails to detect an injected synthetic canary, its authority is immediately revoked. Golden dataset admissions freeze, automated retraining halts, and the critic is demoted to passive logging until recalibrated.


* **Semantic Drift Tracking ($\kappa$):** A continuous 2–5% random sample of scored assets is reviewed asynchronously by human leads. The system tracks Cohen’s Kappa ($\kappa$) inter-rater reliability between human verdicts and the Video-LLM. If agreement drops below $\kappa = 0.80$, admissions are locked automatically.


* **Optimizer Boundary Governance:** Bayesian parameter loops can "game" evaluation metrics (e.g., driving CFG down to its minimum allowable threshold because blurry images yield lower LPIPS delta variance). The meta-loop monitors parameter convergence and alerts engineers if optimization boundaries collapse to edge limits.



---

### 3. Continuous Infrastructure Drift Canaries (`gpu-canary.yml`)

Ephemeral cloud GPU environments (RunPod, Vast.ai, Lambda Labs) are volatile spot markets subject to silent datacenter migrations, driver updates, and bandwidth contention. Passing Gate 0 on Day 2 does not guarantee infrastructure viability in Month 4.

* **Automated Monthly Execution:** On the 1st of every month at 04:00 UTC, `.github/workflows/gpu-canary.yml` triggers an isolated, headless 3-run cold-start benchmark on RunPod.


* **The 3-Run Calibration:** While Gate 0 requires 10 runs to establish initial statistical confidence, the monthly canary uses a 3-run check ($<\$0.25$ total cost) strictly designed for drift detection.


* **Correlated Arbitration Matrix:** The runner evaluates cold ingress, VRAM hydration, 48-frame inference time, total shot cost, and CUDA OOM rates:



| Metric | Green (Nominal) | Yellow (Investigate) | Red (Hard Stop) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Cold Ingress (`s5cmd`)** | $\le 18.0\text{s}$<br> | $18.1\text{s} - 25.0\text{s}$<br> | $> 25.0\text{s}$<br> |
| **VRAM Hydration** | $\le 5.0\text{s}$<br> | $5.1\text{s} - 8.0\text{s}$<br> | $> 8.0\text{s}$<br> |
| **Tensor Compute (48 f)** | $\le 45.0\text{s}$<br> | $45.1\text{s} - 65.0\text{s}$<br> | $> 65.0\text{s}$<br> |
| **Billed Shot Cost** | $\le \$0.060$<br> | $\$0.061 - \$0.080$<br> | $> \$0.080$<br> |
| **CUDA OOM Events** | $0/3$ runs

 | $1/3$ runs

 | $\ge 2/3$ runs

 |

* **Near-Yellow Clustering:** Because network slowdowns directly inflate billed container execution seconds, the arbitrator scans for coupled drift. If ingress latency trips to Yellow and billed cost sits within 5% of its own Yellow limit, the system flags systemic provider decay rather than an isolated network spike.


* **Hard Stop Action:** If any metric hits Red or two hit Yellow, the workflow opens a blocking P0 issue assigned to the Pipeline Engineer, freezing batch renders until compute routing is updated.



---

### 4. How `repo-bot` Automates Phase 5 Operations

`repo-bot` acts as the mechanical edge worker coordinating these maintenance cycles across GitHub, Cloudflare, and the Jules Coding Agent:

* **Shadow Harness Branching:** When `/staging/` reaches its training quota, `repo-bot` provisions an ephemeral benchmark branch, commits the dataset commit hash, triggers the headless shadow canary suite, and comments the A/B comparison report directly onto the promotion PR.


* **Autonomous Drift Remediation via Jules:** When `gpu-canary.yml` flags a provider performance regression (e.g., network ingress slipping past 18s due to dependency bloat), `repo-bot` passes the failed benchmark logs to Jules. Jules runs within an isolated sandbox to audit the Dockerfile, update `s5cmd` concurrency parameters (`--concurrency 64 --part-size 50`), rebuild the test image, and submit a remediation pull request.


* **C2PA Manifest Commits:** Upon optical mastering and final episode export, `repo-bot` collects the cryptographic hashes of every model checkpoint, LoRA version, and human author signature used across the cycle, committing an immutable C2PA provenance ledger entry to the repository registry.The "Premature Infrastructure Trap" is the tendency to engineer sophisticated meta-tooling—such as bespoke AI agents that write code, manage repositories, and manipulate Git ASTs—before validating whether the underlying media pipeline can reliably produce an episode.

In studio architecture, this manifests as "engineering fiction": spending months designing 23-pod organizational structures, Merkle tree canon verifiers, and two-phase commit state machines to avoid the friction of running actual production workloads.

---

### 1. The Meta-Tool Anti-Pattern

Building a custom Workers AI agent hooked directly into the GitHub REST API to programmatically parse, rewrite, and commit codebase files is a textbook premature infrastructure trap.

```text
THE PREMATURE METAPROGRAMMING TRAP
[ Custom Workers AI Code-Writer ] ──► Spends weeks debugging AST parsing & API wrappers
                                  ──► High token spend, edge timeout friction
                                  ──► Pipeline never renders a single frame

VS.

THE PRAGMATIC DISPATCH PATTERN
[ repo-bot (Thin Edge Webhook) ]  ──► Dispatches prompt to Jules Coding Agent API
                                  ──► Jules spins up an isolated, sandboxed cloud VM
                                  ──► Executes tests, edits files, opens PRs natively

```

* **The Anti-Pattern:** Writing bespoke edge middleware that attempts to understand code syntax, resolve file trees, and make low-level Git commits from scratch. This turns your studio into a tooling research lab rather than an animation engine.


* **The Correct Execution:** Offload complex coding, refactoring, and directory scaffolding directly to off-the-shelf coding agents like the **Jules Coding Agent**. Jules already runs inside an isolated, containerized VM with native Git tooling, terminal access, and testing harnesses.


* **`repo-bot`'s Bounded Scope:** `repo-bot` does not attempt to be a software engineer. It remains a lightweight edge webhook handler that does two mechanical tasks: dispatching task prompts to Jules and managing branch tags via standard GitHub REST calls.



---

### 2. The Fatal Waterfall vs. The Risk-Calibrated Gauntlet

Systems architects often fall into the **Waterfall Trap**: attempting to build an entire transmedia ontology and distributed microservice mesh from the bottom up before falsifying core technical assumptions.

```text
                           THE FATAL WATERFALL TRAP
  [ Build Full Hub ] ──► [ Build Mutex / 2PC ] ──► [ Build Linters ] ──► [ Deploy Cloud GPU ]
    (4–6 Months)           (High Complexity)         (Untested ASTs)       (CRASH: OOM / Cost)
                                                                           Sunk Cost: $150,000+
                                                                           Status: Project Scrapped

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

                       THE RISK-CALIBRATED GAUNTLET ORDER
  [ Gate 0: Hardware Spike ] ──► [ Gate 1: Flat Pilot ] ──► [ Gate 2: Tracer Bullet ] ──► [ Gate 3: Thickening ]
    48 Hours / < $10               3–6 Episode Arc / $0       1 Scene End-to-End         Progressive Hub build
    Retires Cloud GPU risk         Retires Human adoption     Proves full assembly       gated strictly on
    and bandwidth economics.       and rework hypothesis.     pipeline in 1 week.        empirical friction.

```

To avoid sinking capital into speculative architecture, the pipeline enforces a four-stage build order:

* **Gate 0 (The 48-Hour Hardware Spike):** Validates the serverless GPU boundary for under $10. It verifies whether `s5cmd` can pull 22 GB of weights from Cloudflare R2 and render a shot in $\le 18\text{s}$ for $\le \$0.06$. If network or virtualization latency breaks this, cloud rendering is abandoned immediately in favor of a local hardware split.


* **Gate 1 (The Flat Pilot):** Validates the human adoption thesis for $0.00. Instead of building Neo4j graph databases or AST linters, the writers' room uses a flat, 3-table SQLite/D1 schema (Facts, Scenes, Dependencies). If writers refuse to declare dependencies in linear prose, the cache invalidation engine is killed before building complex UI dashboards.


* **Gate 2 (The Tracer Bullet):** Forces a single scene completely through the minimal pipe: Screenplay $\to$ Audio TTS Stems $\to$ Remotion Animatic $\to$ Greenscreen Plate $\to$ Final Composite. It proves end-to-end viability before writing an entire season.


* **Gate 3 (Progressive Thickening):** Subsystems (such as Two-Phase Commit Durable Objects, typed state vectors, or automated linters) are unlocked **only** when triggered by concrete operational friction, never on a calendar schedule.



---

### 3. The Walking Skeleton & The Deletion Principle

The core defense against premature infrastructure is **The Walking Skeleton**: an implementation that links the main architectural components together without using the final, fully realized version of any of them.

| Operational Test | The Question to Ask | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Category 1: Present Creative Value**<br> | *"Does this change what actually appears on screen right now?"*<br> | **Build immediately.** (e.g., character LoRA prompts, audio timing manifests, screenplay scripts).

 |
| **Category 2: Future Insurance**<br> | *"Does this change how reliably or scalably something already on screen gets produced?"*<br> | **Defer until friction demands it.** (e.g., meta-repo sync scripts, multi-tenant DO queues, automated changelogs).

 |

By adhering to this distinction, `repo-bot` acts strictly as an insurance utility that is introduced to automate manual Git and Jules tasks **after** those workflows have already been manually proven. It never precedes the creative work.Applying **`repo-bot`** to Spec-Driven Development (SDD) transforms high-level architectural specifications into deterministic code mutations while treating Git repository integrity as an atomic database transaction.

Under this model, the specification is "The Law," Jules is the isolated execution worker in a sandboxed VM, and `repo-bot` acts as the transaction manager with full authority to commit, quarantine, or execute a hard rollback.

---

### 1. The Bounded Spec Intake Protocol

To prevent Jules from hallucinatory wandering or over-engineering, `repo-bot` enforces the strict **Spec-to-Task Pattern**:

```text
[ Architectural Epic / PRD ]
             │
             ▼ (Decomposed into docs/specs/*.md)
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               THE BOUNDED SPEC CONTRACT                │
│                                                        │
│  1. Closed Ledger Scope: Explicitly banned features   │
│  2. Acceptance Criteria: Binary Pass/Fail assertions   │
│  3. Boundary Rules: Zero unapproved dependencies       │
└──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                           │
                           ▼
          [ repo-bot: Pre-Flight Job Ingestion ]

```

* **Closed Ledger Enforcement:** Per studio governance rules, features not in an Epic’s Closed Ledger are unfunded and must not be built. `repo-bot` parses the spec markdown file (e.g., `docs/specs/TASK-02.01.01.md`) and injects hard negative constraints into the Jules task payload.


* **Ephemeral Branch Provisioning:** `repo-bot` never allows Jules to touch `main` or persistent development branches directly. It captures the current `HEAD` commit SHA ($S_{\text{clean}}$) of the target repository, pins it, and cuts an isolated ephemeral branch: `spec/task-02-01-01-jules`.


* **Deterministic Prompt Formulation:** `repo-bot` constructs Jules' instructions to mandate test-first execution: scaffold or update the Vitest test files first, write implementation code second, run the local compilation suite, and push.



---

### 2. The Verification Gauntlet (The "Sense")

Once Jules completes its task run and issues a push notification or webhook to `repo-bot`, the bot does not trust Jules' self-reported success. It intercepts the ephemeral branch and runs a multi-tier verification gauntlet:

| Audit Level | Verification Engine | Failure Criteria | Action on Failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Tier 1: Type & Syntax**<br> | `npm run check:ts` (tsc --noEmit)

 | Any compilation or inference error (e.g., `ts(2322)`).

 | Quarantine branch; trigger retry or abort.

 |
| **Tier 2: Corpus & Relational Integrity**<br> | `npx tsx scripts/compile.ts`<br> | Pass 1 Zod shape fail, Pass 2 foreign-key break, or DAG cycle.

 | Quarantine branch; route structural error.

 |
| **Tier 3: Uncommitted Drift**<br> | `git diff --exit-code compiled/`<br> | Freshly generated JSON diverges from checked-in artifact.

 | Flag uncompiled drift; reject PR.

 |
| **Tier 4: Dynamic Regression Suite**<br> | `npx vitest run tests/`<br> | Any broken existing unit test or defect escape test.

 | Increment attempt counter; analyze trajectory.

 |
| **Tier 5: Cross-Repo Consistency**<br> | `npx tsx scripts/check-versions.ts`<br> | Pinned hashes or interfaces diverge across sibling repos.

 | Immediate hard rejection.

 |

---

### 3. The Hard Rollback Engine ("Atomic Transaction" Mechanics)

If Jules breaks a repository or introduces regression defects, `repo-bot` treats the entire branch session as an abortive transaction and initiates an immediate, hard recovery sequence.

```text
               [ Jules Pushes Ephemeral Branch ]
                               │
                               ▼
               [ repo-bot Runs Audit Gauntlet ]
                               │
                      Did Gauntlet Pass?
                      ┌────────┴────────┐
                      ▼ YES             ▼ NO
             [ Merge / Open PR ]        │
                                        ▼
                         [ Trajectory Analysis ]
                         ├── CONVERGENCE (Attempt < 3) ──► Re-prompt Jules
                         └── DIVERGENCE / ATTEMPT >= 3 ──► EXECUTE HARD ROLLBACK
                                                                  │
             ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 HARD ROLLBACK ACTIONS                  │
│                                                        │
│  1. Force-delete remote branch: git push :spec/branch  │
│  2. Reset local tracking ref to pinned S_clean         │
│  3. Purge orphaned build/package cache artifacts       │
│  4. Restore pre-draft snapshot (bible-state.json)       │
│  5. Post diagnostic postmortem to Slack / ClickUp      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

#### Rollback Execution Steps:

1. **Remote Branch Obliteration:** `repo-bot` immediately deletes the remote tracking branch via the GitHub REST API (`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs/heads/spec/...`), preventing contaminated code from remaining visible in the PR queue or triggering downstream CI workflows.


2. **Point-in-Time State Recovery:** If the task touched shared state ledgers (such as `compiled/bible-state.json`), `repo-bot` invokes the ledger recovery protocol, restoring the pre-task backup snapshot (`fs.copyFileSync('backups/bible-state_pre_task.json', 'compiled/bible-state.json')`).


3. **Local Workspace Reset:** If executed on a runner or local broker, `repo-bot` runs:
```bash
git checkout main
git branch -D spec/task-02-01-01-jules
git clean -fdx

```


This completely purges untracked files, half-installed npm packages, or rogue build artifacts left behind in the workspace.


4. **Transaction Abort Logging:** `repo-bot` records the aborted attempt in its persistent state ledger, increments the failed transaction count, and posts an alert to the `#dev-log` Slack channel containing the exact git diff and compiler error log.



---

### 4. Circuit Breakers & Trajectory Analysis

`repo-bot` must never let Jules enter an infinite "fix-and-break" patch loop. It uses **Convergence vs. Divergence Analysis** to arbitrate retries:

* **Convergence (Allow 1 Retry):** If the failure is a localized syntax miss or an unescaped character, the error is within the same semantic category. `repo-bot` allows Jules one retry cycle by providing the specific compiler error in a micro-prompt.


* **Divergence (Immediate Hard Rollback):** If Attempt 1 failed on a TypeScript type mismatch, and Jules' fix creates a broken relational foreign key or violates a Somatic Invariant vector, the agent is thrashing across boundary layers. `repo-bot` halts the task immediately without burning further cycles.


* **The Three-Cycle Escalation Rule:** Regardless of error type, if a spec is not completely satisfied and verified within 3 execution cycles, `repo-bot` triggers the hard rollback, locks the task status to `BLOCKED`, and escalates directly to the Lead Architect.



---

### 5. Multi-Repo Batch Transactions (Coordinated Specs)

When a specification spans multiple isolated repositories (e.g., updating a shared schema in `goblin-config` or `@snailicid3/consumer-npm` that cascades into `worker-sower-engine`):

1. **Two-Phase Commit Locking:** `repo-bot` locks downstream consumers against updates by staging the changes on synchronized feature branches across all affected repositories.


2. **Isolated Verification:** Jules implements the schema change in Repo A, followed by the consumer update in Repo B.


3. **Cross-Repo Health Check:** `repo-bot` runs `scripts/check-versions.ts` and integration suites across the pair.


4. **All-or-Nothing Rollback:** If Repo A passes all tests but Repo B fails, `repo-bot` does not merge Repo A. It rolls back **both** repositories to their pinned commit SHAs ($S_{\text{clean}}$), ensuring the multi-repo ecosystem never enters a half-migrated, broken state.The **Bounded Spec Intake Protocol** is the architectural firewall `repo-bot` enforces between ambiguous human design requests and the Jules Coding Agent. Rather than treating the LLM as an autonomous developer with open-ended discretion, the protocol treats it as an untrusted, headless compilation worker operating under a strict sandbox.

The protocol guarantees that Jules cannot write code, mutate file paths, or execute commands until the specification is parsed, cryptographically pinned, and bounded into an immutable contract.

---

### 1. The Spec Contract Architecture (`docs/specs/*.md`)

Every task submitted to `repo-bot` must exist as a standalone, version-controlled markdown specification containing machine-parseable YAML frontmatter and an un-gameable execution contract:

```markdown
---
task_id: "TASK-04.02.01"
title: "Implement Somatic Invariant Linter Unit Tests"
target_repo: "@snailicid3/consumer-npm"
base_branch: "main"
owner_pod: "POD-12"
budget_cap_usd: 0.50
timeout_seconds: 600
allow_dependency_install: false
closed_ledger_scope:
  in_scope_paths:
    - "src/linters/somaticLinter.ts"
    - "tests/linters/somaticLinter.test.ts"
  forbidden_paths:
    - "package.json"
    - "package-lock.json"
    - "src/schemas/**"
    - "compiled/**"
---

# MISSION INTENT
Implement full Vitest coverage for the Somatic Invariant Linter to catch banned motor actions at compile-time (T0).

# ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (FALSIFIABLE ASSERTIONS)
1. `npx vitest run tests/linters/somaticLinter.test.ts` passes with exit code 0.
2. `npm run check:ts` passes with zero type errors.
3. Tests assert that an entity with `banned_kinetic_verbs: ['sprint']` throws an explicit `SOMATIC_VIOLATION`.
4. Zero mutations occur outside `closed_ledger_scope.in_scope_paths`.

```

#### Core Contract Primitives:

* **Separation of Intent from Boundaries:** The spec defines the desired outcome (*Commander's Intent*) and the hard operational guardrails, granting the agent tactical freedom in syntax while strictly limiting its operational envelope.


* **The Closed Ledger:** Jules is explicitly forbidden from touching, modifying, or creating files outside `in_scope_paths`. If a proposed solution requires modifying an unauthorized file (e.g., altering a global Zod schema or adding an npm library), Jules must halt and escalate rather than silently mutating dependencies.


* **Falsifiability Against Ground Truth:** Every acceptance criteria must resolve to a binary, deterministic shell command or exit code. The protocol bans qualitative acceptance criteria (e.g., *"clean up the code"* or *"make the error handling robust"*), as LLMs cannot validate subjective assertions.



---

### 2. Pre-Flight Spec Ingestion & Schema Auditing

When a developer, webhook, or script triggers `repo-bot` to run a spec, the Worker does not pass the text straight to an API. It validates the spec through a strict **Zod Contract Parser**:

```typescript
// repo-bot/src/schemas/specContract.ts
import { z } from 'zod';

export const SpecContractSchema = z.object({
  task_id: z.string().regex(/^TASK-\d{2}\.\d{2}\.\d{2}$/),
  target_repo: z.string().min(1),
  base_branch: z.string().default('main'),
  budget_cap_usd: z.number().max(2.00).default(0.50),
  timeout_seconds: z.number().max(900).default(300),
  allow_dependency_install: z.literal(false), // Locked: Jules cannot add third-party code
  closed_ledger_scope: z.object({
    in_scope_paths: z.array(z.string()).min(1),
    forbidden_paths: z.array(z.string()).min(1),
  }),
  acceptance_criteria: z.array(z.string()).min(1),
}).strict(); // Enforces additionalProperties: false

```

```text
               SPECIFICATION MARKDOWN (docs/specs/*.md)
                                  │
                                  ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 repo-bot PRE-FLIGHT AUDITOR                      │
│                                                                  │
│  1. Validate YAML via SpecContractSchema (strict mode)           │
│  2. Verify base commit exists on GitHub API                      │
│  3. Verify targeted files exist in repo tree                     │
│  4. Assert forbidden_paths covers core lockfiles & schemas       │
└─────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                  ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                  ▼ PASSED                        ▼ FAILED
         [ Provision Sandbox ]         [ HARD REJECTION: 400 Bad Spec ]
                                       • Missing binary acceptance criteria
                                       • Missing closed ledger
                                       • Attempts dependency installation

```

If a spec omits a binary acceptance command, targets undefined files, or fails schema validation, `repo-bot` immediately rejects the job before spending any tokens or dispatching Jules.

---

### 3. Cryptographic Workspace Isolation

To ensure that rollbacks are mathematically clean, `repo-bot` provisions an isolated environment via the GitHub REST API before formulating the agent prompt:

```text
[ Remote Repository (main) ]
             │
             ├── 1. Capture S_clean: SHA-256 hash of main HEAD
             │      (e.g., commit c7f4901b...)
             │
             └── 2. Cut Ephemeral Branch:
                    refs/heads/spec/TASK-04.02.01-jules-c7f4901b

```

1. **State Freezing ($S_{\text{clean}}$):** `repo-bot` queries `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/ref/heads/{base_branch}` and stores the exact commit hash as $S_{\text{clean}}$ in its local execution context. This hash serves as the immutable anchor point for rollbacks.
2. **Isolated Namespace:** `repo-bot` provisions a dedicated branch prefixed with `spec/` and suffixed with the short SHA of $S_{\text{clean}}$. Jules is granted read/write permissions **only** to this ephemeral branch; branch protection rules permanently block Jules from writing directly to `main`, `staging`, or production tags.
3. **Dependency Locking:** Because `allow_dependency_install` is locked to `false`, `repo-bot` verifies that the target branch includes a frozen `package-lock.json`. Jules must work strictly within the repository's pre-existing dependencies.

---

### 4. Zero-Trust Prompt Compilation & Jules Dispatch

`repo-bot` translates the verified spec into a prompt assembled using the **Attention Sandwich** pattern, ensuring boundary conditions and test mandates dominate the agent's context window:

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   JULES COMPILED TASK PROMPT                          │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ TOP (SYSTEM LAWS & NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES):                               │
│ • You are an automated implementation worker operating in a sandbox.   │
│ • You are FORBIDDEN from editing any file outside:                     │
│   [src/linters/somaticLinter.ts, tests/linters/somaticLinter.test.ts]  │
│ • You are FORBIDDEN from running 'npm install' or updating lockfiles.  │
│ • If constraints are impossible, stop and emit: CONFLICT_BLOCKED.     │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ MIDDLE (CONTEXT & SPECIFICATION BODY):                                 │
│ • Ingest: docs/specs/TASK-04.02.01.md                                  │
│ • Ingest: Current file contents of src/linters/somaticLinter.ts         │
│ • Objective: Implement the requested somatic linter unit tests.        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ BOTTOM (HARD EXIT TESTS & VERIFICATION MANDATE):                       │
│ • EXECUTE IN ORDER:                                                    │
│   1. Implement the failing test suite in the test file first.          │
│   2. Implement the minimal required logic in the source file.          │
│   3. Run 'npm run check:ts' -> Must return code 0.                     │
│   4. Run 'npx vitest run tests/linters/somaticLinter.test.ts' -> 0.    │
│ • Do not push commits until all test suites pass locally in your VM.   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

* **Negative Guidance Anchoring:** Placing the file path restrictions and command bans at the top prevents context drift, neutralizing the agent's tendency to solve problems by installing arbitrary packages or refactoring unrelated files.


* **Test-First Mandate:** Jules is instructed to write the assertions first, establishing the ground truth locally before touching the production code.


* **The Invariant Tripwire:** The bottom anchor specifies the exact exit commands. The task is not finished when Jules "thinks" the code looks good; it is finished only when the local runner exits with code `0`.



---

### 5. The Job Lease & Idempotency Handshake

To prevent double-dispatches, orphaned runs, and runaway cloud costs, `repo-bot` wraps the Jules API invocation in a lease-tracking lifecycle:

| Protocol Field | Value / Rule | Operational Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`idempotency_key`** | `UUIDv5(task_id + S_clean)` | Prevents duplicate task dispatches if a network timeout occurs during the API call.

 |
| **`lease_ttl`** | 600 seconds (Watchdog alarm) | If Jules hangs in an internal loop, the lease expires and halts further spending.

 |
| **`heartbeat_interval`** | 30 seconds | `repo-bot` polls session telemetry to ensure Jules is actively executing rather than hung.

 |
| **`cost_ceiling`** | Hard-capped at `$0.50` | The session terminates automatically if inference token limits are exceeded.

 |

Once this handshake completes, `repo-bot` dispatches the payload to `POST [https://jules.google/api/v1/sessions](https://jules.google/api/v1/sessions)`. The session ID is recorded in D1 alongside $S_{\text{clean}}$, and the bot enters a passive listening state, awaiting the webhook or test signal that initiates the **Verification Gauntlet**.In Spec-Driven Development, `repo-bot` treats any branch emitted by the Jules Coding Agent as an untrusted, unverified proposal. An autonomous coding agent operating in a sandboxed VM will readily declare a task "complete" based on its own internal rationalization.

The **Verification Gauntlet (The "Sense")** is the deterministic, multi-tier immune system that intercepts Jules' ephemeral branch before it can touch production branches or trigger expensive downstream render queues. A PR cannot merge, and a spec cannot be marked complete, unless it passes through five cascading gates of escalating computational and epistemological depth.

```text
               [ Jules Ephemeral Branch: spec/TASK-XX ]
                                  │
                                  ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   LEVEL 0: STATIC SYNTAX & ZERO-TOKEN LINT       │
│  • tsc --noEmit (Type soundness)                                 │
│  • AST Parse & Regex Triad (Participial chains, crutch density)  │
│  • Slop Filter (Probabilistic suppression of LLM glaze tokens)   │
└─────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Exit 0
                                  ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              LEVEL 1: TWO-PASS CORPUS COMPILER                   │
│  • Pass 1: Zod scalar & shape validation                         │
│  • Pass 2: Relational integrity, FK checks, DAG cycle detection  │
│  • Pass 3: Hash sealing & uncommitted drift detection            │
└─────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Exit 0
                                  ▼
```
